messages:
Camila Reyes: hey folks — for the v1 demo deck refresh we need a clean screenshot of the Console Rollouts view (canary / A/B) for the “Observability + operations” section. who can grab something stable from demo tenant? ideally US + EU tabs visible.

Soojin Lee: +1. the current slide has an old build and it doesn’t show the fallback policy chip. would love a version where we can point at: pinned model, traffic split, guardrails, and the rollback button.

Dylan Brooks: we can do that. question: do you want a “real” seeded rollout with synthetic traffic or a static empty config view? the seeded one is more compelling but we need to make sure the graphs aren’t blank.

Camila Reyes: seeded please, but only if it’s reliable. if it’s flaky we’ll use screenshot + annotated callouts as backup mode.

Chloe Martin: easiest path: use demo project `demo-observability` > Routes > `chat-prod` > Rollouts. it has the canary config + last 24h synthetic load.

Markus Klein: + note: during live demos we usually show the Rollouts list view first (the table w/ status), then click into the specific rollout. two screenshots might be better than one mega shot.

Camila Reyes: yes please. can we get:
1) Rollouts list view (showing `chat-prod` rollout active)
2) Detail view (traffic split + metrics panel)
3) Optional: rollback confirm modal (if it doesn’t reveal anything sensitive)

Dylan Brooks: ok. design question — what exactly should be called out? (so we don’t just dump raw screenshots)

Camila Reyes: annotated callouts for the story beats:
- “Pinned model version” (e.g., `rw-chat-7b@2026-02-10` style)
- “Canary split” (ex: 90/10)
- “Auto fallback policy enabled” (region/model family)
- “Rollback in one click”
- “Error/latency deltas” (the chart or KPI tiles)

Soojin Lee: and a tiny caption we can use in speaker notes: “Operators can ship new model variants with canaries + automatic fallback without changing app code.”

Chloe Martin: heads up: the detail page has some internal IDs if you scroll. keep it above the fold and crop the URL bar.

Leila Farouk: I can run a quick E2E pass to ensure the seeded metrics show non-empty right before you capture. give me 15 mins and I’ll ping when it’s “green”.

Dylan Brooks: perfect. I’ll grab both screenshots once Leila confirms. also, do we have a preferred annotation style? (Figma callouts vs. boxes in the slide)

Camila Reyes: Figma callouts please (numbered dots + short labels). then we can paste into deck as-is.

Figma Bot: Camila Reyes shared a file: “Demo deck v1 – Observability section” https://figma.com/file/REDACTED

Leila Farouk: ✅ seeded traffic looks good now. Rollouts metrics panel has data for p50/p95 latency + error rate. synthetic job is running on the 5-min schedule.

Dylan Brooks: grabbing now.

Dylan Brooks: uploaded 2 PNGs to the Figma frame “Rollouts screenshots (needs callouts)”. cropped URL + org name. I left room on the right for labels.

Camila Reyes: looking — these are great. can we add one more callout for “Compare variants” (the toggle that shows baseline vs canary)? that’s a nice differentiator.

Chloe Martin: yep that toggle is stable. call it “Variant comparison” and point at the baseline/canary overlay.

Soojin Lee: also, can we confirm the naming on the chip is customer-safe? (no internal code names)

Dylan Brooks: it’s using `rw-chat-13b` + date-stamp. no codenames.

Camila Reyes: awesome. I’ll add callouts and route for final review with design + SEs. thanks all :thumbsup:

Markus Klein: please drop the final PNGs in #sales too once done — we’ll use them for backup mode when Console is slow.
